claims.text: The magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type HEAs are governed primarily by chemical short-range order within the ordered hexagonal phase.
The as-deposited alloy forms an ordered single-phase hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited alloy has inherent chemical inhomogeneity.
The as-deposited state results from rapid quenching during deposition.
Annealing at approximately 500°C for 1–4 hours can promote chemical short-range ordering within the hexagonal matrix.
A suitably controlled low-temperature anneal can enhance short-range order without changing the overall phase or inducing secondary precipitates.
Chemical short-range order modulates lattice strain in the hexagonal phase.
Chemical short-range order modulates magnetic-domain coupling and thereby affects transition abruptness and hysteresis.
Low-temperature annealing permits atomic rearrangements that increase chemical short-range order.
Enhanced chemical short-range order relieves microstrain.
Enhanced chemical short-range order reduces pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Reduced microstrain and domain-wall pinning produce a more continuous and broadened magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited baseline has a sharp, large, and highly hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition.
Annealing will moderately reduce the peak magnetic entropy change relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing will distribute the magnetic entropy change over a broader temperature range.
Annealing will significantly reduce hysteresis and improve reversibility during cyclic low-field operation.
The predictions apply under magnetic fields below 0.5 T and within the magnetostructural-transition temperature window.
The predictions require retention of the ordered hexagonal phase without unwanted secondary phases.
Annealing severe enough to cause grain growth or decomposition may invalidate the predicted effects.
Annealing too mild to enhance chemical short-range order may fail to produce the predicted effects.

contradictions.description: The baseline describes arc-melted ingots as examples of samples prepared by rapid deposition methods, whereas arc melting is not a deposition method and does not straightforwardly match the stated as-deposited initial state.
